answer: A work-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable stake and complete a verifiable computation puzzle before its identity can transact. Like a mesa rising above a flat plain, the bond makes each fake identity expensive to raise, while the umber trail of on-chain attestations lets peers trace whether an identity has behaved honestly over its voyage through many transactions. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand stakes and a thousand compute costs, while honest agents pay once and reuse their standing.
